changes.why: Fault 5: the previous 'assert final' changed nothing (287 fails before and after), so this simulator evaluated it like a plain immediate assertion, at the first unsettled moment of the time step. CHK-015 now copies all outputs and i_cpol on each 1->0 transition of i_rst_n. It copies them again on every further change in that same time step, so the copy ends up holding the settled values. The copy is judged at the first event of any later time step (at the latest the next i_clk edge, so before any further rising edge). A copy still waiting at the end of simulation is judged in the final block. Same output list, exact values, every 1->0 transition. Fault 6: the one remaining fail per run is at 5000 ps, the first i_clk edge. There i_rst_n has been 0 since time zero with no 1->0 transition, so this edge is the first point where the reset can act on the flops that drive o_cs_n/o_mosi (REQ-IMP-003/004). The check sampled before that edge settled. CHK-016 now starts checking at a 1->0 transition of i_rst_n, or after the first rising edge in reset when the reset is held from time zero (ENV-008). Edges in the exact time step of a 1->0 transition are skipped (ENV-007/GAP-001); CHK-015 checks the same outputs there after settling. All later rising and falling edges in reset are checked with exact values. The hit counter now counts only edges that are actually checked.

notes:
I changed only verif/sva/nnc_chk_reset.sv; the Python tests from the last round stay as they are. Nothing has been simulated yet, so it is not yet confirmed that faults 5 and 6 now pass.

Why the last change didn't work: CHK-015 failed exactly 287 times both before and after the 'assert final' change. So this simulator runs 'assert final' like a plain assertion, at the first moment of the time step before the outputs have settled. The new check works the same way in any simulator: it copies the outputs on each 1->0 change of i_rst_n, copies them again on every further change in that same time step, and judges the final copy at the next event in a later time step. That checks the settled values in the same time step, before the next rising edge, as the contract asks.

CHK-016 still failed once per run, always at 5000 ps, the first clock edge in the simulation. I think the simulator holds i_rst_n at 0 from time zero without a 1->0 change, so the design's reset flops can only act at that first edge, and the check looked before that edge settled. My guess that the simulator is Verilator fits these numbers but is not confirmed. The check now starts at a 1->0 change of i_rst_n, or after the first rising edge in reset when the reset has been held since time zero. Edges in the exact time step of a 1->0 change are skipped, and CHK-015 checks those values after settling.

I kept the same outputs and exact values, and added no assumptions or $assertoff. One change to the counts: CHK-016 hits now include only edges that are actually checked, so that count will be a little lower than before.
